cues.notes: GDPR Art. 95: the clause bars a second, duplicate obligation with the same objective as the named instrument.
NIS2 Art. 35(2): an express bar on a second fine for the same conduct already sanctioned under the named instrument.
GDPR Art. 94(2): references to the Directive this instrument repeals are redirected to this instrument. Target resolved via repealed_instrument_by_source, not by citation in the clause.
DSA Art. 89(2): references to a named instrument's articles are redirected to this instrument's own provisions. Requires the named instrument to be found inside the matched clause itself.

DSA Art. 2(4)(g): this instrument explicitly yields to the named instrument(s) on the stated matter. clause_end_chars is period-only: the real clause is a single sentence enumerating an (a)-(j) list separated by ';', and the named instrument (GDPR/ePrivacy) sits at list item (g) — stopping at the first ';' truncates the clause before reaching it.

AI Act Art. 2(5): 'shall not affect the application of'. AI Act Art. 2(7): 'shall not affect' with no 'the application of' and a multi-citation list ('Regulation (EU) 2016/679 or (EU) 2018/1725, or Directive 2002/58/EC or (EU) 2016/680') — 'the application of' is made OPTIONAL so both forms fire on one trigger. clause_end_chars is period-only so a long citation list with no ';' boundary still reaches its own final period intact; the same sentence's own trailing 'without prejudice to Article 10(5) and Article 59 of this Regulation' is a self-reference (see _SELF_REFERENCE_RE), which is excluded from target resolution, not a second named instrument.
NIS2 Art. 35(1): a competent authority under this instrument must notify the named instrument's own supervisory authorities — two independent regimes coordinating on one act.

NIS2 Art. 2(14): an activity under this instrument is carried out 'in accordance with' the named instrument's own rules — the named instrument's own rules control that part of the conduct, a structural subordination, not a definitional cross-reference. 'in accordance with' is a weak, generic cue (low confidence) that very often names no instrument at all (e.g. 'in accordance with paragraph 9'); suppress_if_unresolved is set so a reference within the same instrument, or no named instrument at all, never produces a record.
Generic definitional cross-reference: a term used in this instrument has the meaning given to it in the named instrument.
NIS2 Art. 35(1): 'as defined in Article 4, point (12), of Regulation (EU) 2016/679' — a term used in this instrument is defined by an explicit cross-reference to the named instrument's own article.
Synthetic cue: both this instrument and the named instrument apply together, additively, to the same conduct.
Synthetic cue: this instrument supplements the named instrument's obligations within the same matter, rather than replacing or barring them.
Synthetic cue: only one of this instrument or the named instrument applies, determined by the stated scope condition.
Synthetic cue: compliance with this instrument discharges the corresponding obligation under the named instrument.
Synthetic cue: compliance with this instrument does not, by itself, raise a presumption of compliance with the named instrument.

violations: cues[0].suppress_if_unresolved must be a boolean when present
